links.outcome: Hallucination in rationales of multi-agent topologies versus single-LLM baseline across clinical tasks
links.effect: Collaboration improved task performance but not hallucination as a rule; no topology was reliably better than another. Of 36 comparisons, 12 resolved: four decreases and eight increases.
links.quote: We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another.

links.outcome: Hallucination (factuality and faithfulness) within generated clinical rationales across models and systems
links.effect: Of 36 model-system-task comparisons, 12 were resolvable: four decreases and eight increases in hallucination, with no model on both sides. The model, not topology, set the level and direction.
links.quote: The effect differs by model: of the $36$ model--system--task comparisons, $12$ are large enough to resolve --- four decreases and eight increases, with no model on both sides.

unlisted_practices: Self-correction by showing the model its own flagged hallucinations
Scoring hallucination inside generated rationales rather than only final answers

screen.reason: The study empirically tests whether multi-agent collaborative frameworks and self-correction reduce reasoning hallucination in clinical benchmark tasks compared to single LLM baselines.
